reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a purported free Litecoin mining website as a cautionary educational walkthrough, including registration, balance checking, and withdrawal discussion with explicit non-endorsement and loss-risk warnings. The withdrawal control does not establish that cryptocurrency was transferred, that users were paid, or that an additional fee or data request occurred. A separate Telegram giveaway instruction is mentioned, but its terms and outcome do not establish a deceptive mechanism or connect it to the mining platform.

allows users to mine LTC without any deposit or investment
Cryptocurrency mining websites can change, stop paying, or shut down at any time.

opening.argument: Judge, the invitation is more concrete than a general discussion of mining. The description says the website lets users mine Litecoin without a deposit, then offers instructions for registering and withdrawing earnings. It also supplies website links. That joins a low-barrier asset claim to a path for viewers to act on it. A warning that earnings are not guaranteed does not undo the invitation to register and pursue a withdrawal.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that a withdrawal control does not prove payment. But payment is not the point of this concern: the description invites viewers to register, start mining, and seek an LTC withdrawal through the linked website. Likewise, calling the walkthrough educational does not erase that participation path. The warnings qualify the claim; they do not remove the reward-and-action pairing.

citations.quote: How to start mining Litecoin without investment
How to withdraw your LTC earnings

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted steps show what the tutorial covers, not that users will receive Litecoin or that the site demands money or sensitive credentials. The creator explicitly says earnings are not guaranteed and warns that mining sites may stop paying or shut down. The video also advises viewers to stick to the free plan. Links and registration instructions alone do not establish deception.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together: a free-Litecoin earning pitch, shortened website links, a displayed withdrawal flow, and a description urging viewers to join a Telegram channel for giveaways. Each puts an apparently accessible reward beside a way to engage further. The description's warning that mining websites can stop paying makes the payout uncertainty explicit, yet the same material continues to direct viewers toward the website. That combination warrants treating the invitation as a low-barrier reward solicitation, not merely neutral information.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the giveaway's terms and the withdrawal outcome are unproven. That limits what can be claimed about either one, but it does not make the invitation disappear. The material still pairs a giveaway with joining Telegram and a purported free LTC opportunity with a withdrawal interface. The question is whether those reward cues steer participation, not whether a completed payout or later abuse is visible.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those signals do not establish a deceptive mechanism. The withdrawal screen shows an interface, not a paid-out reward or a demand for a fee; the giveaway line supplies no terms or evidence of an adverse outcome. The description explicitly declines to guarantee earnings, payouts, or the third-party platform's legitimacy. Treating uncertainty and external links as proof of a scam goes beyond the supplied evidence.

opening.argument: Judge, the educational framing should be weighed against what viewers are given to do. The description offers a step-by-step path from registration to checking earnings, and says it will cover withdrawing LTC. It then provides website links. In the video, the viewer is told they can register if interested and use the free mining plan. Even with cautions about the platform, this functions as a practical route into a purported free-asset offer. The disclaimer changes the tone of the invitation, but not its direction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to non-endorsement and loss warnings, but those do not settle the role of the walkthrough. Its own description guides registration, mining, balance checking, and withdrawal, while directing viewers to a website link. The conditional advice to register only if interested still supplies a participation route. A demonstration can be cautionary in wording and promotional in effect.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough may make the site accessible, but accessibility is not evidence that it is deceptive. The video explicitly disclaims endorsement, tells viewers to research the platform, and warns them not to invest or deposit. The description also cautions that payouts and legitimacy are not guaranteed. The prosecution identifies an actionable tutorial, but its citations do not show a false payout, a required payment, or misuse of viewer information.
